name: Cherubim
overview: Scripture presents cherubim as powerful, divine beings associated with God's holiness and presence. They are first placed east of the Garden of Eden to guard access to the tree of life with a flaming sword (Genesis 3:24). In the tabernacle, cherubim are intricately crafted figures of gold on the mercy seat, with their wings stretched upward covering it and their faces turned toward one another, symbolizing divine protection and the sacred space of atonement (Exodus 25:18-20). Additionally, cherubim appear as embroidered figures on the tabernacle curtains, emphasizing their integral role in the worship environment (Exodus 26:1, 31).
